info.title: AI Native Call Center API
info.summary: REST and SSE surface of the AI-native call center.
info.description:
The single contract for every HTTP endpoint the platform serves. Spec-first: this document is the source of truth; Go and TypeScript types are generated from it, never the other way around.

Naming follows docs/design/07-naming.md: JSON properties are lowerCamelCase with initialisms treated as words (callId), enum values are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and byte-identical across JSON, TypeScript and the database, timestamps are xxxAt (RFC 3339), durations are xxxSec/xxxMs, booleans are is/has prefixed.

Authentication is an HttpOnly session cookie issued by POST /auth/login. Every mutating request must also carry the X-AICC-Csrf header with any non-empty value. A system integrating without a browser authenticates instead with the X-AICC-Api-Key header, on the operations whose security says so. Errors always use the single envelope {"error": {code, message, params}}; the code is machine-readable and localized by the frontend. That holds for the router's own refusals too: a path this contract does not declare is 404 NOT_FOUND and a method it does not declare on a path it does is 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, both in the envelope — never the SPA's index.html, which a client cannot tell from a successful response.

A separate unauthenticated operations listener (AICC_METRICS_ADDR, default 127.0.0.1:9090) serves GET /metrics, /healthz and /readyz in plain text; it is deliberately outside this contract.

post.description:
One entry point for every call the platform places, told apart by kind.

AI_OUTBOUND originates the customer leg with the DID as caller id; on answer the call bridges to the bot running the DID's flow. Requires SUPERVISOR.

AGENT_OUTBOUND is click-to-dial: an agent's own phone is raised first and the destination is dialled when that leg answers. A signed-in agent may omit extensionNumber and place it from the phone they are signed in at; a supervisor or an API-key caller must name the extension, and the phone at it has to be registered.

Idempotent by client-minted callId either way: a retry with the same id answers isDuplicate instead of redialing.

200.description: The callId was already placed; the response points at the existing call with isDuplicate true.

get.summary: The calls the caller is a party to
get.description: Requires the AGENT role and an agent profile.

The live waiting line, longest wait first, together with the queues it is drawn from. Moves on QUEUE_JOINED, QUEUE_LEFT and QUEUE_COUNT. An agent sees the queues they are staffed on — the same rule that decides which queue events reach their event stream. A supervisor works no line and sees every queue, as they do on GET /calls. The queues are listed even when empty: an agent staffing a quiet line and an agent staffing none at all are different situations, and a list of waiting callers cannot tell them apart.

200.description: Who is waiting, since when, and the queues they are waiting in.

post.summary: Answer the caller's own ringing leg
post.description: Call control acts through the caller's own agent identity: the call id in the path is never authority on its own. Requires the AGENT role.

post.description:
What is hung up depends on what the caller has.

An agent has a leg on the call and ends that leg: they leave the conversation, and whether the call itself survives is the switch's business. They must be a party to it — a call id in the path is never authority on its own.

A supervisor, an administrator and an API-key caller have no leg of their own, so the leg is found by the call instead: the one at the extension, hung up exactly as if the person at that phone had. The bridge collapses and the switch releases the far end. They may do this to any call, which is how a call placed by a system for an agent who never signed in gets ended — nobody is a party to it, so nobody could end it through an agent's rule. A call with no leg at an extension answers 409.

202.description: The switch accepted the command; the outcome arrives on the event stream.

post.description: Sends the far end to a queue extension or number. Requires the AGENT role and being a party to the call. Transferring, holding and retrieving are refused on an INTERNAL call with OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_CALL_TYPE (409): one extension calling another is two people on a line, not a call being handled — there is no third party to pass it to and no queue to put it back into.

202.description: The switch accepted the command; the outcome arrives on the event stream.

post.summary: Send DTMF tones to the other party
post.description: Emits tones towards the far end, which is what reaches an IVR the caller was transferred to. Requires the AGENT role and being a party to the call.

202.description: The switch accepted the command; the outcome arrives on the event stream.

post.summary: Listen to, whisper into or join an agent's call
post.description: Raises the supervisor's own phone and attaches it to the named agent's leg with the switch's eavesdrop: LISTEN hears both sides silently, WHISPER is heard by the agent only, BARGE is heard by everybody. Requires SUPERVISOR. The phone is the supervisor's own — the one they are signed in at as an agent, else the one bound to their agent identity in configuration; an account with no phone is refused with CONFLICT (409), as is an agent who is not on the call. A supervisor holds one monitoring leg at a time: a second request ends the first, which is how a mode is changed. The supervisor's leg is not a party to the call: it appears in no event and no CDR, only in the audit log.

202.description: The switch accepted the command; the supervisor's phone answers by itself.

Stream counters and the trunks the switch holds. Requires ADMIN. Liveness and readiness live on the separate operations listener, outside this contract.

Server-sent events, one SseEvent envelope per data: line, the type mirrored on the event: line and the global seq on the id: line. Scope comes from the authenticated identity; ?types= may only narrow what that identity would already receive. Reconnection resumes from Last-Event-ID (or ?lastEventId=); a resume point older than the replay ring triggers a SYSTEM_RESET event telling the client to refetch snapshots. A comment heartbeat (": hb") flows every 15 seconds. The connection has no timeout; it ends with the client.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated SseEventType names to narrow the stream.

parameters.name: lastEventId
parameters.description: Resume point for clients that cannot set the Last-Event-ID header.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The browser's own resume point, echoed from the id: line.

200.description: The stream. Each data: line is one SseEvent; per-type payload shapes live in components/schemas under the Sse*Payload naming convention (SseCallbackEventPayload, SseSystemResetPayload).

get.summary: A call's journey through the queues
get.description:
Every movement the switch reported for this caller, oldest first: the queues joined, each agent offered the call, and how it left. The CDR answers how the call ended; this answers how routing behaved on the way there — a call offered thirty-three times and one offered once are the same abandoned row in the CDR.

Supervision, not an agent's own view: these rows name colleagues who were offered the call and did not take it.

200.description: The call's queue movements, oldest first, possibly empty — a call that never entered a queue has none.

get.description:
Every mutating request that succeeded, newest first. Written by middleware rather than by each handler, so a new write endpoint is audited the moment it exists.

ADMIN only: the trail names accounts and carries what their requests contained.

parameters.name: actionPrefix
parameters.description: Only actions starting with this, matched literally. The action is "METHOD /route/template", so a prefix selects by method, by resource, or by both — "DELETE " for every deletion, "PUT /api/v1/queues" for queue edits.

patch.summary: Attach business data to a live call
patch.description: Merges business data into a call that is already running — an order number a backend resolved after the call arrived, a case the agent opened while talking. RFC 7386 semantics: a value replaces the key, null removes it, keys the patch does not mention are left alone. Requires the AGENT role and being a party to the call; a system integrating with this rides such a session. The whole patch applies or none of it does: if it would take the call past 32 keys the call is left exactly as it was and the answer is 409, naming the keys that would not fit. Data that moved is announced to everyone on the call as CALL_USER_DATA.

200.description: The call’s business data after the patch.

get.description: Requires ADMIN. Tokens are not included.

post.description: Requires ADMIN. Deliberately out of reach of AICC_API_KEY: that credential places and ends calls, and letting it also choose where the platform sends finished calls would let a leaked key exfiltrate every one of them (design 09 §10).

201.description: The stored subscription, without its token.

get.description: Requires ADMIN.

put.description: Requires ADMIN. Omitting authToken leaves the stored one alone.

200.description: The stored subscription, without its token.

delete.description: Requires ADMIN. Its deliveries go with it.

get.description: Newest first, for diagnosing what a subscriber was told and what came back. Requires ADMIN.

cookieSession.name: aicc_session
cookieSession.description: Opaque session token issued by POST /auth/login. The cookie name is configurable (AICC_SESSION_COOKIE); aicc_session is the default. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax.

csrfHeader.name: X-AICC-Csrf
csrfHeader.description: Anti-CSRF header required on every mutating request (any method other than GET, HEAD, OPTIONS). Any non-empty value passes; requiring a custom header forces a CORS preflight on cross-origin callers. Missing header: 403 FORBIDDEN.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-AICC-Api-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: Shared secret (AICC_API_KEY) for a system placing calls without a browser session. It authenticates the deployment's integrator, not a person, and is accepted only on the operations that say so. A request carrying it needs no session cookie and no X-AICC-Csrf header — CSRF protects a cookie, and this caller sends none. Unset AICC_API_KEY leaves the machine path closed.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed: unparseable body or an invalid identifier. Codes VALIDATION_FAILED, USER_DATA_TOO_LARGE.

Unauthorized.description: No session or the session expired. Codes SESSION_EXPIRED, INVALID_CREDENTIALS.

Forbidden.description: The identity lacks the role, the CSRF header is missing, the account is suspended, or the account is not an agent. Codes FORBIDDEN, USER_SUSPENDED, NOT_CALL_PARTY.

NotFound.description: The target does not exist. Codes NOT_FOUND, CALL_NOT_FOUND.

Conflict.description: The request collides with current state. Codes CONFLICT, EXTENSION_IN_USE, EXTENSION_ASSIGNED_TO_AGENT, EXTENSION_POOL_EXHAUSTED, LAST_ADMIN, AGENT_ALREADY_LOGGED_IN, AGENT_NOT_LOGGED_IN, AGENT_NOT_IN_WRAP_UP.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The body parsed but a field is missing or invalid. Code VALIDATION_FAILED; params.field names the offender when known.

BadGateway.description: The switch did not take the call. Code SWITCH_DOWN.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency is unreachable. Codes STORAGE_DOWN, SWITCH_DOWN.

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable, translatable failure identifier. The frontend renders errors.<CODE>; the backend never localizes.

Error.description: The single error envelope body: an error code plus interpolation params. Message is diagnostic English, never shown to end users.

params.description: Interpolation parameters for the localized message, e.g. {"field": "extensionNumber"}.

Role.description: Ranked roles; a higher role passes every lower gate (ADMIN > SUPERVISOR > AGENT).

locale.description: Preferred UI locale (lowercase BCP 47 subtag) or null when the user has not chosen one.

NotReadyReason.description: Why an agent is NOT_READY. LOGIN, AFTER_CALL_WORK, SYSTEM and SUPERVISOR are set by the platform, never chosen by the agent.

Availability.description: The single word that answers: could this agent take a call, and if not, why.

Presence.description: One agent's presence. enteredAt is when this state began, which for WRAP_UP is when the call ended — after-call work has no deadline, it ends when the agent files it.

agentId.description: Whose presence this is. The cockpit needs it to tell its own party from the other side on a call where both parties are agents — an internal extension-to-extension call reaches both of them through /calls/mine, and picking the first party that happens to carry an agentId shows one agent the other one's state.

wrapUpCallId.description: The call the agent is doing after-call work for. Set while availability is WRAP_UP and kept until the next call is wrapped, so a filing made after the agent has moved on still lands on the right call.

WrapUpRequest.description: What the agent confirms for the call they just finished. Both fields are optional: the record already exists with a default disposition, and pressing Done with neither is an agent saying the defaults are right.

dispositionCode.description: A code from GET /dispositions; omitted keeps the one on the record.

note.description: Omitted keeps the note on the record.

CurrentWrapUp.description: The after-call work waiting on this agent: the record the platform opened for the call they just finished, as it stands. It survives a page reload, which is how a cockpit knows to keep asking.

createdAt.description: When after-call work began for this call.

AgentLoginRequest.description: Sign-in takes no arguments in the ordinary case: the agent-to-extension binding is static configuration, so the platform signs the agent in at the phone they are bound to.

extensionNumber.description: Overrides the bound extension. Omit it to use the agent's configured phone; an agent with no binding is refused with CONFLICT.

reason.description: Omitted or empty defaults to BREAK.

RosterEntry.description: One agent on the supervisor roster.

extensionNumber.description: The phone the agent is signed in at right now; absent when signed out.

currentCallId.description: The live call the agent's leg is on, present while isOnCall is true. What a supervisor's monitor request names.

callcenterName.description: The identifier the switch knows this agent by.

defaultExtensionId.description: The extension bound to this agent in configuration. Unlike extensionNumber it survives sign-out, and it is what administration edits.

defaultExtensionNumber.description: The bound extension's number, resolved for display.

Agent.description: One agent's configuration, as administration stores it. Presence is not part of it — the roster carries that.

userId.description: The account this agent identity belongs to. One user has at most one agent identity.

AgentWrite.description: Create or update an agent identity. An extension may be bound to at most one agent; binding one that is taken is refused with CONFLICT.

userId.description: Required on create and ignored on update: an agent identity never moves between accounts.

callcenterName.description: Reaches the switch as an identifier: no spaces, @ or quotes.

defaultExtensionId.description: The phone this agent signs in at. Null unbinds them, after which they cannot sign in.

User.description: An account, with the agent identity and phone that belong to it when it has them.

agentId.description: The ACD identity, present for an account that takes calls. An administrator has none — they are a user but not an agent, and the two are not the same thing.

callcenterName.description: How the switch names this agent. Stamped when the identity is created and never renamed afterwards: it is what mod_callcenter, its tiers and every historical record know them by.

extensionNumber.description: The phone bound to this account, allocated from AICC_EXTENSION_RANGE when the account was created. Absent for an account with no phone.

UserStatus.description: Whether the account may sign in. A suspended account is refused on its next request, not at its next login: the session check reads the account, so suspending takes hold at once.

UserCreate.description: A new account. An AGENT or SUPERVISOR also gets an ACD identity and a phone allocated from the extension pool, in the same transaction: an account that takes calls is not usable without them, and half-provisioning is not a state anybody could act on. An ADMIN gets neither.

username.description: Letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen. Narrower than the column, because an agent's switch-side name is derived from it and mod_callcenter cannot hold a space, an @ or a quote.

password.description: The initial password. The account can be given a new one at any time by an administrator; nothing here can read it back.

UserUpdate.description: The account as it should now read — a whole replacement, so read it, change what you meant, and send all of it back. Promoting an ADMIN to a call-taking role provisions the identity and phone they lack; demoting one never removes them, because their state history and filed wrap-ups hang off that identity.

PasswordReset.description: A password an administrator sets on somebody else's account. Every session opened with the old one is revoked, so a reset ends access rather than merely changing what would work next time.

CallType.description: Caller-perspective call type, stamped at creation and immutable across transfers.

PartySnapshot.description: Immutable view of one call leg.

isBotLeg.description: True for the leg the switch dialled towards the AI gateway. A caller talking to the bot is on a call with two legs and only one person, and nothing else in this object distinguishes that leg from an agent it has no agentId for.

isMuted.description: True while the switch is silencing this leg's microphone.

QueueFacts.description: A call's passage through a queue.

CallSnapshot.description: Immutable view of a live call: the aggregate plus its parties.

userData.description: Business data attached to the call; merge-patched, survives transfers.

StaffedQueue.description: A queue the reader works, whether or not anybody is waiting in it. An agent's own line; every queue for a supervisor.

name.description: Switch-safe identifier: no spaces, @ or quotes.

slaThresholdSec.description: The queue's answer target; a wait past it is a breach. 0 means none is configured.

WaitingCall.description: A caller waiting in a queue: joined and not yet bridged to anybody. Ordered longest wait first, which is who the queue serves next.

slaThresholdSec.description: The queue's answer target; a wait past it is a breach. 0 means none is configured.

queues.description: The queues the reader works, listed whether or not anybody is waiting in them. A line with nobody in it is an answer, not an absence.

digits.description: The tones to emit, in order. 0-9, A-D, * and # are the only DTMF symbols there are.

MonitorMode.description: LISTEN: the supervisor hears both sides and is heard by nobody. WHISPER: the agent also hears the supervisor. BARGE: both parties hear the supervisor.

agentId.description: Whose leg to attach to. A call may carry two agents (an internal call), so the leg is always named.

CreateCallRequest.description: Ask the platform to place a call. Which fields apply depends on kind.

callId.description: Client-minted id making the request idempotent: a retry with the same id answers isDuplicate instead of redialing.

kind.description: AI_OUTBOUND hands the answered customer to the bot; AGENT_OUTBOUND rings an agent's phone first and dials the destination when they pick up. Both produce a call of type OUTBOUND.

did.description: AI_OUTBOUND only: the DID whose flow and caller id the call uses.

extensionNumber.description: AGENT_OUTBOUND only: the extension whose phone is raised first. A signed-in agent may leave it out — the phone they signed in at is used — and may not name another's. A supervisor or an API-key caller has no phone of their own, so they must name one.

language.description: AI_OUTBOUND only: overrides the DID's language when set.

callbackId.description: AGENT_OUTBOUND only: the callback this call is placed to keep. It must be CLAIMED by the caller — a dial for a callback somebody else holds, or nobody does, is refused with 409. The call id is noted on the callback at once and its outcome is copied back when the call ends; the callback itself stays CLAIMED until the agent closes it.

isDuplicate.description: Present and true when the client-minted callId was already placed; the response points at the existing call.

Extension.description:
A number a phone can register at, and the agent it belongs to.

Nothing else: a queue is dialled rather than registered as, and reaches its callers through queues.extNumber, which this table never touches.

agentId.description: The agent whose phone this is. Read here and written by binding the agent to it: the binding lives on the agent so the database can still refuse to delete a phone somebody works at, which is a guard an incident put there.

ExtensionWrite.description: Create or update a phone. An account's phone is allocated when the account is created, so this is the entry for automation and for a handset that belongs to nobody in particular. An empty password leaves an existing one alone.

password.description: Write-only: required on create, optional on update (empty keeps the current one). Never returned; the only reader that needs it is the switch.

ExtensionSecret.description:
A phone's SIP registration password, in clear.

It is stored in clear deliberately (D4): the a1-hash alternative is bound to the SIP realm, this deployment's realm follows the host address, and that address has already moved twice — a hash cannot be recomputed, so every phone would need a new password and every registered agent would be knocked off mid-shift. The cost of that choice is this endpoint, and the price of this endpoint is that reading it is recorded.

Strategy.description: How a queue picks among the agents staffing it, in platform vocabulary; the switch spelling is a boundary translation.

Overflow.description: Where an unserved caller goes. BOT_FLOW and FORWARD need a target.

TierRules.description: How a queue widens its agent search over time.

Queue.description: A waiting line served by agents.

name.description: Switch-safe identifier: no spaces, @ or quotes.

QueueWrite.description: Create or update a queue. Omitted fields take server defaults (strategy LONGEST_IDLE_AGENT, overflow ANNOUNCE_HANGUP, mohSound $${hold_music}, tierRules.waitSec 300, isEnabled true, isRecordingEnabled true).

name.description: Switch-safe identifier: no spaces, @ or quotes.

extNumber.description: Omit it and the next free number in the queue pool (AICC_QUEUE_RANGE) is allocated — which is what a form should do, because whoever adds a queue is asking for a queue, not for 7004. Supplying one is for a deployment that has to match numbers it does not own.

QueueAgent.description: One agent's place on a queue.

DID.description: An external number and which way calls go through it. A number callers can reach answers with a bot flow; the fallback queue takes the caller when the bot cannot. A number used only for dialling out has no flow to bind, because nobody calls it.

language.description: Lowercase BCP 47 subtag, at most 8 characters. Sets the greeting, the prompt language and the voice; it does not select a provider, which is a deployment-wide setting.

allowInbound.description: Callers can reach this number. An inbound number answers with a flow, so one is required.

allowOutbound.description: This platform can place calls from this number.

isDefaultOutbound.description: The number an agent's call goes out from when nothing names one. At most one number in the deployment carries this, enforced by the database rather than by whoever remembers to clear the last one.

DIDWrite.description:
Create or update a number. Omitted fields take server defaults (language en, inbound, isEnabled true, isRecordingEnabled true).

A number must go somewhere: at least one direction. An inbound one needs a flow, and only an outbound one can be the default a call goes out from.

allowInbound.description: Callers can reach this number. An inbound number answers with a flow, so one is required.

allowOutbound.description: This platform can place calls from this number.

isDefaultOutbound.description: The number an agent's call goes out from when nothing names one. At most one number in the deployment carries this, enforced by the database rather than by whoever remembers to clear the last one.

FlowSpec.description:
One complete conversation flow in the v2 flow DSL: the bot's persona, rules and voice, the phases a call moves through, the tools each phase allows, and the transitions between them.

The document is deliberately opaque to this contract. Its dialect is defined and validated by the server's loader, which is the same code a live call parses the published revision with; restating that shape here would be a second definition, free to drift from the one that actually runs. A spec the loader rejects is refused with 422 and every problem it found, so what can be stored is exactly what could run.

Flow.description: A flow's identity and publication state. The draft is what an author edits; a revision is an immutable copy taken at publish time. Calls only ever run the published revision, so an edit in progress can never change what a live number does.

slug.description: Stable identifier chosen at creation and never changed: it is the key `aicc flowadd` updates an existing flow by.

publishedRevisionId.description: The revision live calls run. Absent while the flow has never been published — a number pointing at it reaches no bot.

publishedAt.description: When the current revision went live. Absent while nothing is published.

hasUnpublishedChanges.description: The draft differs from the published revision, or nothing is published yet. Callers hear the revision, so this is the gap between what is written and what answers the phone.

FlowRevision.description: A publish that happened: which snapshot, when, and why. The stored spec is not served — a revision is a record of publication, and reading one back is rollback, which this surface does not offer.

note.description: Why it was published; empty when none was given.

isPublished.description: This is the revision live calls run.

FlowDetail.description: One flow: what it is, what its draft says, and every time it has been published.

FlowCreate.description: A new flow, stored as a draft. Creating does not publish: a number pointing at an unpublished flow reaches no bot, so going live stays a separate, deliberate act.

FlowDraftWrite.description: Replaces the draft wholesale. The slug is not editable: it is the identity automation updates the flow by, and renaming it would quietly create a second flow on the next `aicc flowadd`. Live calls are unaffected until the draft is published.

note.description: Why this revision was published; kept with the snapshot.

UserData.description: Business data attached to the call: the order, ticket or case this conversation is about. Flat key/value only, values strings, because this is read as a list of labelled facts and nothing renders a nested object. At most 32 keys, each value at most 1024 bytes of UTF-8; over either limit the request is refused with 400 USER_DATA_TOO_LARGE rather than truncated — a screen showing half a customer's details, with no sign the other half was sent, is worse than a gap. Omitted and {} mean the same thing: no business data. It never reaches the switch.

UserDataPatch.description: An RFC 7386 merge patch over a call's business data: a value replaces the key, and null removes it. Keys the patch does not mention are left alone. Setting a key to the value it already holds changes nothing and is announced as nothing. The same bounds apply to the result, so a patch that would take the call past 32 keys is refused whole with 409 rather than partly applied.

UserDataResponse.description: The call's business data after the patch, and what the patch moved. The lists are sorted and name movement only: a key set to the value it already held appears in neither.

CDRStatus.description: How the call concluded. There is no MISSED status: abandonment is a missedReason on an ANSWERED row, because the bot answered first.

MissedReason.description:
Why the caller went unserved, decided from recorded facts rather than a hangup cause, caller's own phase first. Absent when the call was not missed — there is no empty member.

It describes one journey: an inbound caller who wanted a person. Every value is a place on that journey, so the field is deliberately absent on the calls that were never on it — an outbound call this platform placed, a call between two extensions, and an inbound call that never reached a queue or an agent (a number this deployment does not serve, or a caller who hung up on a direct extension before it was picked up). Those did not go unserved; they did not go. Why they ended is hangupCause, which says it exactly, and a NO_ANSWER row with no missedReason is that and not a gap. Counting missed calls therefore means counting this field, never counting NO_ANSWER.

Leg.description: One hop of the call's journey, for the journey summary.

CDR.description: One finished call. totalSec always equals the sum of its parts.

answeredAt.description: When the call became billable: the moment the leg facing whoever charges for it was answered. Inbound, that is the caller's own leg and the 200 OK the switch sent towards the carrier; on a call an agent placed it is the leg dialled out, since the agent's own phone picks up in front of them and nobody bills for that. Set even on a call the bot served and no agent took, which is billed all the same. Between two extensions it records the answer while billSec stays 0.

ringSec.description:
Seconds spent ringing an agent. For an answered call, from the answering leg's creation to its bridge; for one nobody answered, from the first leg dialled to the last one released — a queue that re-offers dials a fresh leg each time, so no single leg holds the answer.

Not a segment of the call to be added to the others: on a queued call it lies inside queueWaitSec, and on a call that never queued there is no queue window for it to lie inside, so it overlaps whatever else was happening. See totalSec.

botSec.description: Seconds the caller spent with the bot, ending when they actually left it — after any closing sentence has finished playing, not when the transfer was decided.

queueWaitSec.description: Seconds the caller waited in queue, from joining to being bridged to an agent, or to leaving if they never were. Ringing happens inside this window, so ringSec is a sub-interval of it rather than an addition to it.

talkSec.description: Seconds an agent had two-way media with the caller, measured from the bridges on the agent legs and unioned across them, so a call passed from one agent to another counts both stretches once. A leg that answered without a bridge — an auto-answer phone in front of nobody, a codec mismatch — contributes nothing. Hold counts as talk.

billSec.description: Billable seconds: answeredAt to endedAt. This is the carrier's number, not the agent's — a call the bot answered and nobody took is still billed. 0 when the call was never answered, and 0 between two extensions, which nobody charges for.

totalSec.description:
Seconds from startedAt to endedAt, the whole life of the call including the time before it was answered. Not the billable duration; see billSec.

The other durations do not partition this one. botSec, queueWaitSec, ringSec and talkSec each measure a stretch of the call in its own terms and those stretches overlap — ringing happens inside the queue's window, most obviously — so subtracting them from totalSec to find unaccounted time yields a number that means nothing. Adding them can exceed totalSec on a perfectly ordinary call. The three the caller passes through in order — botSec, queueWaitSec, talkSec — are consecutive and do fit.

isContained.description: True when the bot finished the conversation without a human.

tech.description: Technical residue (switch causes and the like); never business data.

wrapUp.description: The after-call work filed for this call: the requesting agent's own on GET /cdrs/mine, the primary agent's (else the latest) elsewhere. Absent when nobody filed one.

WrapUp.description: One agent's after-call work for one call. The platform opens it when the call ends — a default disposition, an empty note — and the agent confirms it; isConfirmed is what separates a record somebody looked at from one nobody has. The label is captured at filing time so the record survives later edits to the vocabulary.

isConfirmed.description: True once the agent pressed Done. False means the defaults are still standing.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, for paging.

TranscriptLine.description: One thing said or done on a call, in either phase. seq is dense per call and is both the sort key and the backfill cursor.

content.description: TEXT carries {text}; TOOL_CALL and TOOL_RESULT carry the tool name and arguments or result.

Recording.description: One stored audio artifact of a call.

backend.description: Storage backend, e.g. fs or s3.

CDRDetail.description: One finished call with everything it left behind, in one round trip.

Callback.description: A promise to call somebody back, taken by the bot and kept by an agent.

handledBy.description: The user working or having closed the callback.

lastAttemptCallId.description: The most recent call placed from this callback.

lastAttemptAt.description: When that call was placed; once it ends, when it ended.

lastAttemptStatus.description: How that call went, absent while it is still up.

status.description: DONE means the promise was kept; DISMISSED means it no longer needs keeping.

Contact.description: A customer record. The phone number is the key the cockpit looks a caller up by, so it is unique.

lastCallAt.description: When this number last appeared on a finished call, either side. Absent when it never has.

ContactWrite.description: Create or update a contact. Omitted fields are stored empty on create and left unchanged on update.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, for paging.

Disposition.description: One word an agent can file a call under. The code is stable; the label is what agents read and is the operator's to change.

DispositionCatalog.description: The wrap-up vocabulary: every enabled disposition, in display order.

QualityReview.description: A reviewer's scoring of one recording.

scores.description: Per-criterion scores; null when the reviewer submitted none.

Overview.description: KPI aggregates over the report window.

AgentToday.description: One agent's own day, over the window (default: local midnight to now). The totals are served beside the averages so every number on the screen can be checked against them.

callsHandled.description: Calls this agent answered, counted from the ledger's primary agent.

talkSec.description: Total talk time on those calls.

wrapUpSec.description: Total after-call work, from the presence history; an open wrap-up counts up to now.

signedInSec.description: Total time signed in, whatever the state; the denominator of occupancy.

avgHandleSec.description: (talkSec + wrapUpSec) / callsHandled — the average handle time. 0 when no call was handled.

avgWrapUpSec.description: wrapUpSec / the number of wrap-ups begun in the window. 0 when there were none.

occupancyPct.description: (talkSec + wrapUpSec) / signedInSec as a percentage, 0 when signed out all window.

wrapUpsOpened.description: After-call records opened in the window — one per call this agent finished.

wrapUpsConfirmed.description: How many of them the agent confirmed.

confirmedPct.description: wrapUpsConfirmed / wrapUpsOpened as a percentage — how much of the day's after-call work somebody actually looked at. 0 when nothing was opened.

queueId.description: Null aggregates the calls that never entered a queue.

oldestSeq.description: Oldest sequence still in the replay ring; a client behind it must resync.

trunks.description: The gateways the switch holds. Empty when the switch cannot be reached.

SseEventType.description: Every event name on the stream. PARTY_* are leg-scoped, CALL_* call-scoped, SYSTEM_* stream-control. DEVICE_* report a phone on two independent axes and name one transition each: REGISTERED/UNREGISTERED say whether a SIP registration exists, REACHABLE/UNREACHABLE whether the registered phone still answers the switch's OPTIONS ping. A registered phone that stops answering is the agent-side failure that matters most — it looks exactly like a working one — so it has a name of its own rather than borrowing UNREGISTERED.

SseEvent.description: One envelope on the event stream. Call events repeat enough context (callType, userData) for a screen-pop without further requests. In SSE framing the envelope is the data: line, the event: line carries type, and the id: line carries seq.

seq.description: Global order. Echo the last seen value as Last-Event-ID to resume.

payload.description: Type-specific body. Stable shapes are named Sse*Payload in this document; the rest are registered as they harden.

SseBotSessionStartedPayload.description: Payload of BOT_SESSION_STARTED: the conversation is running, which is not the same as the bot's leg being up. The leg answers first and the model session is opened afterwards, and it can fail — the caller is then rescued to a queue. Until this arrives, a caller on an answered bot leg may be talking to nothing.

flowId.description: The published flow revision answering this call. Not otherwise knowable while the call is running; the ledger only says so afterwards.

SseCallUserDataPayload.description: Payload of CALL_USER_DATA: the call's business data changed, and these are the keys that moved. The resulting data itself is on the envelope's userData, as it is on every call event — this names what is different about it, so a screen can highlight the change without diffing. Both lists are sorted, and a key set to the value it already held appears in neither: what is announced here is movement, not merely that a write arrived.

changedKeys.description: Keys that were added or given a new value.

SseQueueJoinedPayload.description: Payload of QUEUE_JOINED: a caller entered the queue named on the envelope's queueId.

SseQueueLeftPayload.description: Payload of QUEUE_LEFT: the caller left the queue, whether answered, abandoned or timed out. cause and cancelReason are the queue's own words, stable codes rather than display text.

SseQueueCountPayload.description: Payload of QUEUE_COUNT: how many callers are waiting in the queue named on the envelope's queueId, published whenever that number moves.

longestWaitAt.description: When the longest-waiting caller joined; absent when nobody is waiting.

SseSystemResetPayload.description: Payload of SYSTEM_RESET: the resume point aged out of the ring; refetch snapshots before tailing again.

Speaker.description: Who said a line. CUSTOMER is the person who called, whichever leg carries them; BOT is the AI; HUMAN_AGENT is a logged-in agent answering after a transfer.

TranscriptSource.description: Where a line came from. MODEL is the conversational engine's own transcript of the AI leg; ASR is a separate recognition of streamed audio.

TranscriptionState.description: Health of live transcription for a call, as the agent should see it. ENDED is the snapshot's answer for a call that is over: it is produced by GET /calls/{callId}/transcript rather than by the transcription actor, which is why the actor's own mirror of these values does not name it.

SseTranscriptPayload.description: Payload of CALL_TRANSCRIPT: one line of the conversation, from either phase of the call. seq orders the transcript within the call and is unrelated to the envelope's transport seq. A partial carries isFinal false and no seq, because it has no place in the order until it is final.

SseTranscriptionStatePayload.description: Payload of CALL_TRANSCRIPTION_STATE: whether the agent is seeing everything that is being said, and if not, which side is missing. reason is a stable code, never display text.

CallTranscript.description: A page of a call's transcript, plus where to resume. isLive says whether more is still coming, so a client knows to tail rather than poll.

QueueEventName.description: What happened to a caller in a queue. OFFERED repeats: one call can be offered to several agents, or to the same agent several times, before it is bridged or abandoned.

QueueEvent.description: One movement of a caller through a queue.

agentId.description: The agent this movement concerns: who was offered the call, or who it was bridged to. Absent for movements that concern no one in particular.

waitMs.description: How long the caller had been waiting when this happened. Zero where the movement does not measure a wait.

AuditEntry.description: One recorded change: who did what to which thing, and from where.

actorId.description: Absent for an action no signed-in account performed.

actorUsername.description: The account's name at read time. Absent when the account has since been deleted — the row keeps the id either way, so a cleaned-up roster does not erase what its accounts did.

action.description: The method and the route template that matched, e.g. "PUT /api/v1/queues/{queueId}". The route template rather than the path, so the value is stable and greppable and cannot drift from the routing table.

targetKind.description: What kind of thing was acted on, derived from the last path parameter. Empty where the request named no instance.

detail.description: What the request carried. Fields whose name reads like a secret are stored as "[redacted]" — a marker rather than an omission, because a field that was sent and not kept is a different fact from one that was never sent.

ip.description: The peer address the request came from. Absent where it could not be determined.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, for paging.

Trunk.description: A gateway as the switch currently holds it. Read, never written: a gateway is defined in the switch's own profile configuration and this application does not write that file. What the product can usefully answer is whether the trunk is there.

profile.description: The sofia profile it lives on.

address.description: Where the switch sends calls for it.

state.description: The switch's own word — REGED, NOREG, DOWN, FAIL_WAIT. Passed through rather than mapped: a trunk down for a reason the switch has a name for should say that name.

isUp.description: Whether the switch would place a call through it now. A NOREG gateway is dialable as it stands — an IP trunk never registers by design — so registration is not the question.

WebhookSubscription.description: A place finished calls are delivered to. authToken is never returned: the customer supplied it and already has it, so there is nothing to hand back (design 09 §8).

name.description: Operator-facing label. A list of URLs is unreadable.

isEnabled.description: False stops deliveries without losing the subscription or its history, which is what an operator wants when a customer's endpoint is down.

hasAuthToken.description: Whether a token is configured. The token itself is never served; this says only whether there is one, so a screen can show a subscription that would reach an endpoint with no credential at all.

WebhookFilter.description: Which finished calls this subscription wants. A key present means the CDR's field must be one of the listed values; keys are ANDed; an absent key does not constrain, so {} means every call. Deliberately not an expression language: the keys are a closed list checked when the subscription is written, because a filter validated at delivery time is discovered as a customer receiving silence (design 09 §5).

status.description: CDR status: ANSWERED, NO_ANSWER, BUSY, FAILED.

isContained.description: Calls the bot handled without ever reaching a person.

WebhookSubscriptionWrite.description: Create or update a subscription. authToken is write-only: send it to set or replace it, omit it to leave it as it is, send an empty string to clear it.

authToken.description: The customer's own credential, presented as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every delivery. It is theirs, not this deployment's AICC_API_KEY, which points the other way and must never be used here (design 09 §8).

WebhookDelivery.description: One attempt-set at delivering one revision of one call's CDR to one subscription.

deliveryId.description: Travels to the customer as X-AICC-Webhook-Id; their deduplication key.

revision.description: 1 for the first delivery of a call. A later, fuller CDR replacing one already sent produces revision 2, and the receiver's rule is last-revision-wins per callId — deliveries are concurrent, so the number decides, not the arrival order.

lastStatusCode.description: Absent until an attempt has been made.
